artifacts.summary: 7-phase plan (12h) building the per-repo Sapience activation surface: MCP-registration triad, 11 permission grants, 5 hooks, docs, and end-to-end acceptance of all five verification items.

memory_candidates.content: When a plan mirrors an existing extension's shipped script triad, check whether the model achieves its durability by writing a file the new task is forbidden to touch. The lean extension's install-lean-lsp-session-hook.sh registers its SessionStart hook in BOTH ~/.claude/settings.json and ~/.dotfiles/config/claude/settings.json, because `hooks` is a home-manager ENFORCED key (the set is [_NOTE,env,hooks,model,permissions,statusLine] in modules/home/core/dotfiles.nix) that is reset from the .dotfiles source on every switch whenever that source carries a `hooks` key. A task scoped to forbid .dotfiles edits therefore inherits a silent durability gap from the precedent it is told to mirror: the user-level registration works until the next `home-manager switch` and then vanishes with no error. The reset is conditional on `$src | has($k)`, so the gap closes only if the source drops the key entirely - which it will not when other entries (an inhibitor hook, another extension's hook) still live there. Plan it as a named residual with an installer warning plus verifier detection, not as a working mechanism.
